Template Syntax & Tokens

Anza Server Templates have one construct: the {{token}} placeholder. It is replaced with the value of the matching parameter. The same syntax works in the Rust, TypeScript and Python engines.

What You Get

SyntaxPurposeExample
{{variable}}Inserts the parameter's value as is<h1>{{title}}</h1>

There are no loops, conditionals or filters. Build lists and optional sections in your handler and pass the resulting HTML in as a parameter (see Slotted Child Content).

Rules:

  • Whitespace inside the braces is trimmed: {{ title }} is the same as {{title}}.
  • An unclosed {{ or an empty {{}} is an error when the templates load.
  • A missing parameter renders as an empty string.

Variable Substitution

Simple values are substituted directly into template placeholders:

<div class="user-profile"> <h2>{{username}}</h2> <span class="user-role">{{role}}</span> <time datetime="{{joined}}">Member since {{joined}}</time> </div>

When provided with data:

{ "username": "alex", "role": "Maintainer", "joined": "2026-01-15" }

Renders as:

<div class="user-profile"> <h2>alex</h2> <span class="user-role">Maintainer</span> <time datetime="2026-01-15">Member since 2026-01-15</time> </div>

Escaping & Security

Values are not HTML-escaped. Whatever string you pass is written into the output unchanged, which is what lets a parameter carry pre-rendered HTML. Any value that comes from users must be escaped by your code before rendering:

  • & → &amp;
  • < → &lt;
  • > → &gt;
  • " → &quot;
  • ' → &#x27;

For example, in Python use html.escape(value, quote=True); in TypeScript or Rust, a small helper that replaces those five characters.

Slotted Child Content

When composing nested templates or docks, render the children first and pass the HTML in as a parameter:

<dock-feed class="articles-feed"> <template shadowrootmode="open"> <slot></slot> </template> {{articles}} </dock-feed>

In the backend handler (Rust):

let card = engine.get("feed/card.html")?; let articles_html = articles .iter() .map(|a| card.render(a)) .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()? .join("\n"); let mut params = HashMap::new(); params.insert("count".to_string(), articles.len().to_string()); params.insert("articles".to_string(), articles_html); let html = engine.get("pages/home.html")?.bind(&params)?;

Form Actions & URL Interpolation

Variables can be interpolated into attribute values for links, form actions and data attributes. Escape them (and URL-encode path segments) when they come from users:

<div class="card-footer"> <a href="/article/{{slug}}" class="read-link">Read article &rarr;</a> <form method="POST" action="/articles/{{id}}/delete"> <button type="submit">[delete]</button> </form> </div>

Performance Best Practices

  1. Load templates at startup: Setup(...).run() reads and parses every template once; renders never touch the filesystem.
  2. Keep logic out of markup: format, sort and filter data in your handler before rendering.
  3. Render fragments for streaming: use Fragment (or engine.render_fragment / renderFragment) to get a signed envelope, then encode it as an SSE event. See Real-Time Streaming.
